decisions.reason: As a newly launched safety shoe line in the firm’s core category, it is close to existing capabilities and would likely be retained while management gathers more performance feedback.
The comfort insole complements the main footwear business and is inexpensive to carry, so a large firm with some slack would usually keep it unless early results clearly disappointed.
The supportive insole fits the existing product system but faces some portfolio overlap with other insoles, so it is somewhat more exposed to later pruning yet still likely to be kept for now.
An ergonomic safety shoe series with its own page signals strategic importance and strong fit with the firm’s innovation-led core business, making withdrawal unlikely after only one year.

Firefighter and rescue boots are a more specialised niche, so aspiration shortfalls are more plausible, but the product still aligns with the firm’s protective-footwear competence and would likely remain on the market.
A moulded insole featured on the home page suggests active support and perceived potential, so behavioral-theory logic points to continued experimentation rather than early withdrawal.
